description: Ingest of reviewed candidates from scripts/60_authority_domain_sweep.py (issue #75). Covers substantive hits for Moon, Nadeau, Ralston, and additional Ikeda corroboration found while validating the sweep. Incidental-mention and false-positive candidates remain on file under data/reference/sweeps/ and are intentionally not ingested.

metadata.notes: Encyclopedia of Aikido entry: b.1940, 7th dan, began late 1950s, 2+ years at Aikikai Hombu early 1960s, spiritual/meditative emphasis, AANC leader, Aikido of Mountain View address.

sources.title: Aikido Association of Northern California (Encyclopedia of Aikido)

metadata.notes: Established c.1974, largest aikido organization in California, 50+ dojos, directly affiliated with Aikikai Hombu. Principal instructors: Robert Nadeau, Frank Doran, William Witt.

b.1923, 3rd dan, author (The Ultimate Athlete), VP of Esalen Institute, past president of Association for Humanistic Psychology, 'first taught by Robert Nadeau', chief instructor of Aikido of Tamalpais.

1931-2001, US Marine Corps veteran and South San Francisco police officer. Early NorCal aikido pioneer; taught aikido in South San Francisco 1960-1972. 'Among his students was Robert Nadeau' — Nadeau's pre-Japan aikido teacher.

sources.title: Interview with Aikido Authors Bob Noha and Laurin Herr: Robert Nadeau and the Art of Transformation, Part I

metadata.notes: Noha began under Nadeau in Mountain View 1966 after the dojo wrote the Aikikai requesting an instructor; Nadeau dispatched fresh from Japan. Herr: Cornell 1971, Hombu shodan 1976, Hikitsuchi student in Shingu, met Nadeau at a 1999 Monterey workshop. Corroborates Nadeau's Human Potential Movement circle: Michael Murphy (Esalen co-founder; Golf in the Kingdom embeds Nadeau's teachings), George Leonard (student), Bob Frager, Esalen teaching.

sources.title: Interview with Aikido Authors Bob Noha and Laurin Herr: Robert Nadeau and the Art of Transformation, Part II

metadata.notes: Aikido: The Art of Transformation co-authored by six Nadeau students: Bob Noha, Laurin Herr, Teja Bell, Richard Moon, Susan Spence, Elaine Yoder. Project initiated by Teja Bell during the pandemic; 82 collected stories; Nadeau opened his scrapbook. Nadeau bio per Herr: tough kid, Marine Corps, police officer, Karate/Judo before aikido. Photo caption: Nadeau with Julian Silverman at Esalen, 1970s.

Moon-authored contributed article in Aikido Journal. States he entered aikido 'over four decades' earlier and was a yoga instructor at the time; 'going into my fifth decade' in 2014. Evidence of standing in the aikido press; primary for Moon's own words and timeline.

sources.title: The Skills, the Art, and the Path by Richard Moon

metadata.notes: Second Moon-authored AJ article. Mentions teaching 'a blending exercise to some Bosnians after the war' — corroborates his Bosnia conflict-resolution facet.

sources.title: Aikido: Past, Present and Future (contributed editorial by Patrick Cassidy)

metadata.notes: Cassidy's contributor bio states he trained 7 years with Morihiro Saito in Japan, was Dojo-cho of Aikido of Fresno, and 'continued his training with Peter Ralston, Robert Nadeau Shihan and Richard Moon Sensei'; later founded Aikido Montreux and the Evolutionary Aikido Community. Single published source documenting the Ralston/Nadeau/Moon teaching triangle through a common student.

First virtual Aikido Bridge seminar, 3 May 2020 via Zoom, hosted by Aikido Shimbokukai, 130+ participants. Instructors: Wendy Whited, Andy McLean, Dorin Marchis, Gary Marks, Liese Klein, and Hiroshi Ikeda (closing session). Independent corroboration of the Bridge series and Ikeda's Shimbokukai affiliation.

sources.title: Interview with Evolene Premillieu: Aikido for Tomorrow

metadata.notes: Premillieu moved to Boulder specifically to train under Ikeda and Tres Hofmeister; Aikido for Tomorrow created at Ikeda's encouragement, inaugural event hosted at Boulder Aikikai Feb 2020. Photo caption corroborates Ikeda at the 10th Anniversary Aikido Bridge seminar in San Diego (~2015, consistent with 2005 founding).

sources.title: Interview with Aikido of Madison Cofounders Robin Cooper and John Stone, Part I

metadata.notes: Cooper/Stone began aikido 1974 in Madison WI, trained under Saotome from 1977 (incl. San Rafael AANC summer camp 1977), opened Aikido of Madison 1984. Photo caption: 'Robin Cooper, Hiroshi Ikeda, and John Stone posing in their Aikido of Madison in the 1980s' — visit corroboration, not affiliation. They train with Ikeda and Tomoleoni (Shimbokukai) currently.

nodes.label: Robert Tann

metadata.notes: 1931-2001. US Marine Corps veteran, South San Francisco police officer. Early Northern California aikido pioneer; taught aikido in South San Francisco 1960-1972. Among his students was Robert Nadeau (pre-Hombu).

nodes.label: George Leonard

metadata.notes: b.1923, 3rd dan Aikikai, author (The Ultimate Athlete), VP Esalen Institute, past president Association for Humanistic Psychology, chief instructor Aikido of Tamalpais. First taught aikido by Robert Nadeau.

nodes.label: Patrick Cassidy

metadata.notes: 6th dan Aikikai. Trained 7 years under Morihiro Saito in Japan; Dojo-cho of Aikido of Fresno; continued training under Peter Ralston, Robert Nadeau, and Richard Moon; founder of Aikido Montreux and the Evolutionary Aikido Community.

nodes.label: Robin Cooper

metadata.notes: Co-founder of Aikido of Madison (1984). Began aikido 1974 in Madison WI; trained under Saotome from 1977; currently trains with Ikeda and Tomoleoni (Shimbokukai).

nodes.label: John Stone

metadata.notes: Co-founder of Aikido of Madison (1984). Began aikido 1974; trained under Saotome from 1977; nanadan.

nodes.label: Aikido of Madison

metadata.notes: Founded by Robin Cooper and John Stone; Saotome-lineage, Shimbokukai-affiliated training circle.

nodes.label: Aikido Association of Northern California (AANC)

metadata.notes: Largest aikido organization in California, 50+ dojos, directly affiliated with Aikikai Hombu. Principal instructors: Robert Nadeau, Frank Doran, William Witt (AJ Encyclopedia).

nodes.label: COVID-19 Aikido Bridge Seminar (virtual)

metadata.notes: First virtual Aikido Bridge seminar during COVID-19 lockdown. Six instructors: Wendy Whited (Inaka Dojo), Andy McLean (Chishin Dojo, UK), Dorin Marchis (Musubi Dojo, Romania), Gary Marks (Denver Aikikai), Liese Klein (New Haven Aikikai), Hiroshi Ikeda (Boulder Aikikai, closing session).

nodes.label: AJ Encyclopedia: Nadeau b.1940, 7th dan, Hombu early 1960s, AANC leader

metadata.claim_text: Aikido Journal Encyclopedia: Nadeau (b.1940), 7th dan Aikikai, began aikido in the late 1950s, studied more than two years at Aikikai Hombu in the early 1960s, known for spiritual/meditative emphasis; leader in the Aikido Association of Northern California.

nodes.label: AANC principal instructors: Nadeau, Doran, Witt

metadata.claim_text: The AANC (est. c.1974, largest aikido organization in California, 50+ dojos, direct Aikikai Hombu affiliation) names its principal instructors as Robert Nadeau, Frank Doran, and William Witt.

nodes.label: Robert Tann was Nadeau's pre-Japan aikido teacher

metadata.claim_text: Robert Tann (1931-2001), Marine Corps veteran and South San Francisco police officer, taught aikido in South San Francisco 1960-1972; Robert Nadeau was among his students — i.e., Nadeau's pre-Hombu teacher.

nodes.label: George Leonard was first taught aikido by Nadeau

metadata.claim_text: George Leonard (b.1923, Esalen VP, author of The Ultimate Athlete) was 'first taught by Robert Nadeau' and became chief instructor of Aikido of Tamalpais.

nodes.label: Nadeau's Human Potential Movement circle (Murphy, Leonard, Frager, Esalen)

metadata.claim_text: Nadeau developed relationships with Human Potential Movement figures in 1960s Northern California: Michael Murphy (Esalen co-founder; 'Golf in the Kingdom' embeds Nadeau's teachings), George Leonard (became his student), and psychologist Bob Frager; he taught at Esalen for many years.
metadata.notes: Noha/Herr are affiliated (Nadeau's own students and biographers) — treat as attributed recollection in article usage.

nodes.label: Aikikai dispatched Nadeau to Mountain View dojo (~1966)

metadata.claim_text: The Mountain View dojo wrote to the Aikikai requesting an instructor; the Aikikai dispatched Nadeau, who arrived fresh from Japan where he had trained with the founder (~1966, per Noha who began under him there in 1966).

nodes.label: Nadeau pre-aikido: Marine Corps, police officer, Karate/Judo

metadata.claim_text: Per Herr recounting Nadeau's own narrative: grew up a 'tough kid', served in the Marine Corps, became a police officer, practiced Karate and Judo before aikido. Secondhand biographical detail — corroborate against the Art of Transformation book itself.

nodes.label: Art of Transformation co-authored by six Nadeau students incl. Moon

metadata.claim_text: Aikido: The Art of Transformation was co-authored by six Nadeau students — Bob Noha, Laurin Herr, Teja Bell, Richard Moon, Susan Spence, Elaine Yoder — begun during the pandemic at Teja Bell's initiative, built from 82 collected stories and Nadeau's personal scrapbook.

nodes.label: Moon authored two contributed articles in Aikido Journal (2014, 2015)

metadata.claim_text: Richard Moon has published at least two contributed articles in Aikido Journal ('Bestowed Mission' May 2014; 'The Skills, the Art, and the Path' Oct 2015) — evidence of standing as a published voice in the aikido press. Primary source for his views, not independent coverage.

nodes.label: Moon was a yoga instructor when he started aikido (~early 1970s)

metadata.claim_text: Moon states he was a yoga instructor when he entered aikido and had been practicing 'over four decades' as of 2014 (start c. early 1970s).

nodes.label: Moon taught a blending exercise to Bosnians after the war

metadata.claim_text: Moon states he 'taught a blending exercise to some Bosnians after the war' — self-reported corroboration of his Bosnia conflict-resolution work.

nodes.label: Cassidy trained under Ralston, Nadeau, and Moon

metadata.claim_text: Patrick Cassidy's AJ contributor bio states he 'continued his training with Peter Ralston, Robert Nadeau Shihan and Richard Moon Sensei' — one published source documenting a common student of all three subjects.

nodes.label: First virtual Aikido Bridge seminar (May 2020) hosted by Shimbokukai, Ikeda closing

metadata.claim_text: The first virtual Aikido Bridge seminar (3 May 2020) was hosted by Aikido Shimbokukai via Zoom with 130+ participants and six instructors; Ikeda closed the seminar — independent corroboration of the Bridge series and of the Ikeda-Shimbokukai relationship.

nodes.label: Ikeda at Aikido of Madison in the 1980s (visit, not affiliation)

metadata.claim_text: MAYTT photo caption documents Ikeda at Aikido of Madison with co-founders Cooper and Stone in the 1980s; they continue to train with Ikeda — corroboration of a long seminar relationship. NOT affiliation evidence.

nodes.label: Premillieu trained under Ikeda in Boulder; AfT created at his encouragement

metadata.claim_text: Premillieu moved to Boulder to train under Ikeda and Tres Hofmeister; Ikeda encouraged her to create Aikido for Tomorrow, whose inaugural Feb 2020 event Boulder Aikikai hosted.

nodes.label: Saotome taught at AANC San Rafael summer camp 1977

metadata.claim_text: Cooper/Stone recount Saotome teaching at the Northern California Aikido Association's San Rafael summer camp in 1977 — corroborates the San Rafael camp circuit era (cf. Kayla Feder interview).

metadata.notes: Tann taught aikido in South San Francisco 1960-1972; Nadeau among his students — Nadeau's pre-Japan teacher. Consistent with encyclopedia: 'began practice late 1950s, 2+ years at Hombu early 60s'.
Encyclopedia: 'first taught by Robert Nadeau'. Noha/Herr corroborate Leonard became Nadeau's student and an aikido teacher in his own right.
Chief instructor of Aikido of Tamalpais, Mill Valley CA — establishes Tamalpais as Nadeau-lineage context for Ikeda's documented visits there.
Cassidy's AJ contributor bio: 'continued his training with ... Robert Nadeau Shihan' while Dojo-cho of Aikido of Fresno.
Same bio: '...and Richard Moon Sensei'.
Same bio: 'continued his training with Peter Ralston...' — published evidence that Cassidy trained under all three subjects.
Moved to Boulder specifically to train under Ikeda (and Tres Hofmeister) at Boulder Aikikai.
AANC: established c.1974, 50+ dojos, direct Aikikai Hombu affiliation; Nadeau named a principal instructor alongside Frank Doran and William Witt.
MAYTT report; Ikeda gave thanks to attendees/hosts at close.
Moon is one of six co-authors of Aikido: The Art of Transformation (Nadeau biography). NOTE: duplicate work node work:e45a467deb9c9e11 exists — dedupe ticketed.
